stories.excerpt: Victor Wembanyama has found a new way to shoot in order to give his hands a rest and prevent future blisters. Now Wemby seemed too preoccupied with the issues within his own dome to worry about wreaking havoc in anybody else’s. stories.title: Spurs use strong fourth quarter to put away Clippers at home
stories.excerpt: The San Antonio Spurs overcame a season-high 21 turnovers, using a strong fourth quarter to defeat the Los Angeles Clippers 124-112 at the Frost Bank Center on Thursday night in the penultimate game of their three-game home stand. stories.title: Houston Rockets vs. Denver Nuggets game preview
stories.excerpt: Tonight is the third game of Houston’s NBA Cup journey. A loss here eliminates Houston from moving to the next round (I think technically it doesn’t but in reality it does). A win would put Houston in a decent spot to advance but would still need some help. Basically, you shouldn’t be looking at NBA Cup standings at this point. That meant they were tired for the game in Toyota Center, but they still decided to play everyone. In this situation, it’s Houston coming in at the tail end of a four-game road trip. I’d expect the game to go in Denver’s favor with that fact, especially with Houston having potentially zero big bodies to pester Nikola Jokic defensively or make him work on the other end of the court. stories.title: Knicks 102, Timberwolves 99: Knicks Cut Down Wolves
stories.excerpt: After couple great resume wins that included the first time in Minnesota Timberwolves franchise history where they defeated the same team, twice in a row, on back-to-back nights, the home stand continued with a familiar face back in town. stories.title: Rapid Recap: Trail Blazers 124, Bucks 114

stories.title: Russell Westbrook shows there’s no hard feelings in Los Angeles with heartfelt statement
stories.excerpt: Russell Westbrook spent four seasons in Los Angeles. In 2021, the nine-time All-Star joined the Lakers via a trade with the Wizards. After two seasons with the Purple and Gold, Westbrook signed with the Clippers and spent another two years in Tinseltown. This holiday season, Westbrook has kept a close connection to the Los Angeles community. Three years ago, Westbrook and the Clippers opened a community basketball court at Jesse Owens Park in South Los Angeles where he grew up. On Thursday, Westbrook returned to his hometown to hand out Thanksgiving meals and groceries. Not long before Westbrook joined the Clippers, his 18-month tenure with the Lakers featured a fractured relationship with superstar LeBron James, locker room tension and organizational fallout. But the franchise moved on and so did he. In August, the 2016-17 MVP announced his retirement after 18 seasons in the league. It was a shocking decision given many of his former teammates believed Westbrook could have continued his NBA career. While Westbrook’s time with the Lakers seemingly ended in dramatic fashion, it’s evident he still holds the city near to his heart.

stories.title: Knicks eke out lucky win in Minnesota after fourth-quarter collapse
stories.excerpt: MINNEAPOLIS — Style points don’t matter. “For ‘Dancing with the Stars,’ ” Karl-Anthony Towns said. “For us, at the end of the day, as long as we win, this team is just trying to stack the number on the left side.” The Knicks did stack another win in that left standings column. The Knicks led by 12 entering the fourth quarter and then quickly went up by 16 after Tyler Kolek’s 4-point play to start the quarter. It appeared they had stabilized a bit when Towns’ driving layup and Mikal Bridges’ subsequent 3-pointer put the Knicks back up by nine. A free throw, a Gobert alley-oop and an Ayo Dosunmu 3-pointer later, and the Knicks led by just three. Towns then was called for an offensive foul, and Bridges badly missed a jumper on the Knicks’ next offensive possession. The Timberwolves couldn’t find a quality shot, though, with Dosunmu and Gobert both missing shots. Minnesota never got closer than three. LaMelo Ball badly missed a potential game-tying 3-pointer with under 10…

stories.title: Warriors finish winless road trip with lopsided loss to Grizzlies
stories.excerpt: It turns out that Steph Curry is pretty important to the Golden State Warriors success. When the Dubs head out on a five-game road trip just over a week ago, they did it with an eight-game winning streak and all the momentum in the world. And then, just a few minutes into the five-city trip, Curry suffered an oblique injury, and a few hours later, the Warriors lost to the Houston Rockets. What followed was brutal: a 38-point loss to the San Antonio Spurs, a 21-point defeat at the hands of the New Orleans Pelicans, a 22-point loss to the upstart Dallas Mavericks, and finally, on Thursday night, a 28-point loss to the surprisingly great Memphis Grizzlies. The silver lining, if you’re into that sort of thing, is that the Warriors looked the best that they have since Curry was injured, despite losing 126-98. The execution was the best it had been in a while, but ultimately, an astounding lack of shooting did the Dubs in. As had been the case in all of the other Curry-less games, the Warriors got off to a comically slow start. They trailed 5-0, and then 8-2, and Steve Kerr’s first timeout came when the Warriors trailed 13-4 just a few minutes in, as the team was racking up the turnovers. Even the good news was bittersweet: Charles Bassey scored the first seven points for Golden State, but also collected three quick fouls. Still, the Warriors were executing well … mostly. They couldn’t resist turning the ball over, with eight giveaways in the first quarter alone, but they were…

stories.title: San Antonio vs. Los Angeles, Final Score: Spurs outlast Clippers in 124-112 win
stories.excerpt: It didn’t take long for the Spurs to get back on the winning track. The Silver and Black didn’t amaze, but they took care of business at home against a shorthanded Clippers team. The 124-112 score might suggest that it was a comfortable victory, but it was mostly a close game in which the more talented squad simply stepped on the gas late to close it out. The Spurs, facing an inferior opponent after the loss to the Pistons but missing Dylan Harper, didn’t look as dominant as it would have been ideal to start the game. The pace wasn’t great, and neither was the decision-making for most of the first half. Defensively, they had good stretches but also moments in which they allowed dribble penetration without much resistance or left shooters open. It wasn’t the strong bounceback many were hoping for, but because of their tremendous talent, they managed to lead by 14 points at one point in the second quarter. Unfortunately, the lead disappeared as the bench had one of its all-too-familiar poor runs. In all fairness, however, the second unit wasn’t the only reason why the home team only led by three at the break, as the starters didn’t return with the energy required to pull away. Some good moments showed the high ceiling the Silver and Black have, but it wasn’t a particularly inspiring first half. The Clippers deserve credit for capitalizing on the at times lackadaisical and downright sloppy play from the Spurs, but a lot of San Antonio’s wounds in the opening two frames were…

stories.title: Lakers vs. Kings Preview: Time to start another winning streak
stories.excerpt: After witnessing their nine-game losing streak come to an end, the Lakers (13-3) have the opportunity to get back in the win column on Friday against the Sacramento Kings (1-13). stories.title: NBA Trade Rumors: Is a potential trade target emerging for Utah?
stories.excerpt: According to Zach Lowe, teams are calling the Chicago Bulls to trade for Tre Jones. You can listen to the podcast here. View Link Lowe says Tre Jones is the best backup guard in the NBA, which is exactly what the Utah Jazz need. Considering he is making $8M a year, he would fit into Utah’s TPE from the Walker Kessler deal. In that scenario, Utah wouldn’t even need to send a player. Although they could send Isaiah Collier in a potential deal, he would be a high-upside play for the Bulls. Jones is averaging 10.9 points, 3.4 assists, 2.1 rebounds, and 1.1 steals this season. His advanced numbers are pretty solid, and if you put him on the Jazz with the talent surrounding him, he could really flourish. We’ll see if Jones ends up being a player who gets moved, but it’s something that would make a lot of sense for the Utah Jazz if they’re looking to solidify their backup guard position. Why do I mention the Jazz at all? Well, we know they are having internal conversations about Kyrie Irving. If that’s the case, then it’s a safe bet they’re talking about Jones as well. Maybe they are one of those teams that’s already called about Jones? No way to know for sure, but it’s time to start paying attention to the rumor mill.

stories.title: NBA Trade Rumors: Jazz connected to superstar guard?
stories.excerpt: The Utah Jazz have given internal consideration to Kyri Irving, according to Ian Begley. stories.title: Karl-Anthony Towns letting his Knicks play speak loudest in face of uncertainty
stories.excerpt: MINNEAPOLIS — In his own words, this should be an uncomfortable situation for Karl-Anthony Towns. Regardless, it’s produced some of the best basketball of his career.
